title: Twisted-arrow coupling and its slice comparisons
statement:
Use quasicategories, simplicial operators and Kan mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], left fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and join slices of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. For a simplicial set $K$, write $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ for the simplicial set with the same degree-$n$ sets and operators $d_i^{\mathrm{op}}=d_{n-i}$ and $s_i^{\mathrm{op}}=s_{n-i}$ in degree $n$. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory. Define $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)_n$ to be the maps $N([n]^{\mathrm{op}}\star[n])\to\mathcal C$, where the ordered join places every member of the first ordered set before every member of the second. For $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, its operator is precomposition with $N(\theta^{\mathrm{op}}\star\theta)$. Restriction to the two blocks gives
$$\lambda:\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)\longrightarrow\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal C.$$
This is a left fibration. For a vertex $x$, define $(\mathcal C_{x/})_n$ by maps $\Delta^0\star\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$ constant at $x$ on the first point, with restriction operators and projection to the last block. Collapsing the first block gives an equivalence
$$\mathcal C_{x/}\longrightarrow\{x\}\times_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)$$
of quasicategories over $\mathcal C$. Collapsing the second block gives the dual equivalence
$$(\mathcal C_{/y})^{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)\times_{\mathcal C}\{y\}$$
over $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Both maps carry the identity-arrow vertex to the identity-arrow vertex. The constructions and maps commute with simplicial functors carrying the chosen vertices to the chosen vertices.

source.place: Kerodon Construction 8.1.1.1 and Notation 8.1.1.6 (03JK), Proposition 8.1.1.11 (03JQ, left fibration), Proposition 8.1.2.10 (03K0, coslice comparison), and its opposite-category dual. Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. Read online; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: For each monotone map $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, the join map $\theta^{\mathrm{op}}\star\theta$ preserves both ordered blocks. Its composite with the join map for $\psi:[\ell]\to[m]$ is the join map for $\theta\psi$. Precomposition therefore gives all simplicial identities and commutes with restriction to the two blocks. Thus $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)$ is a simplicial set and $\lambda$ is a simplicial map.

Fix $n\geq1$ and $0\leq k<n$ and a lifting square for $\Lambda_k^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ against $\lambda$. The base simplex supplies maps on both pure blocks of $J_n=\{\bar n<\cdots<\bar0<0<\cdots<n\}$. For each face $d_j$ with $j\neq k$, the upper horn map supplies a map on the face obtained by deleting the pair $\bar j,j$. On intersections these maps agree by the simplicial identities and the lifting square. The prescribed domain is exactly $H_{n,k}$ in [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-join-horn], so that node's finite filtration extends this map to $N(J_n)$: at each stage apply the defining inner-horn filler of $\mathcal C$, and glue the extension across the displayed pushout. The resulting $(2n+1)$-simplex restricts to the prescribed base and horn and is the required lift. This proves the left-fibration assertion with the full range $0\leq k<n$. The base $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal C$ is a quasicategory: opposite reverses the horn index from $j$ to $n-j$, and products fill inner horns coordinatewise. To fill an inner horn in $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)$, fill its image in this base and then use the just-proved lifting property. Hence $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)$ is a quasicategory as well.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.1.15, paired-face subcomplex, followed by Proposition 8.1.1.11 and Corollary 8.1.1.12

proof.text: Fix $x$ and put $P_x=\{x\}\times_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)$. Its second-block projection $P_x\to\mathcal C$ is a left fibration: regard any lifting square as a square for $\lambda$ with constant first coordinate $x$ and use Step 2; the lift stays in $P_x$. Filling an inner horn first in $\mathcal C$ then over it shows $P_x$ is a quasicategory. Applying [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] to $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and then reversing ordered vertices identifies $((\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}})_{/x})^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\mathcal C_{x/}$, and turns its right-horn range $0<j\leq n$ into the left-horn range $0\leq n-j<n$. Thus $\mathcal C_{x/}\to\mathcal C$ is also a left fibration of quasicategories. The order map $[n]^{\mathrm{op}}\star[n]\to[0]\star[n]$ constant on the first block and the identity on the second induces by precomposition a simplicial map $u:\mathcal C_{x/}\to P_x$. It commutes with the second-block projections, and in degree zero is the identity on the represented edges, including $\operatorname{id}_x$.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.2.10, commutative diagram and left-fibration hypotheses; explicit collapse map

proof.text: The identity edge at $x$ is an equivalence, witnessed by its degenerate inverse triangles. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final] in $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$: this edge is final in $(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}})_{/x}$. It is therefore initial in its opposite $\mathcal C_{x/}$. To check this last duality with the fixed right-pinched mapping convention, use the homotopy equivalences to the arrow mapping spaces supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. For any quasicategory $D$, simultaneous reversal of the parameter simplex and of $\Delta^1$ identifies $U_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,b)$ with $U_D(b,a)^{\mathrm{op}}$. The realizations of $K$ and $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ are homeomorphic by reversing barycentric coordinates on each simplex; the defining face and degeneracy identifications agree with that reversal. Thus weak contractibility of the arrow mapping spaces is preserved, and the pinch comparison transfers it back to the right-pinched mapping spaces. This establishes initiality in exactly the convention of the item. The realization-cylinder theorem [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] turns the simplicial inverse homotopies of the pinch maps into continuous homotopies, and [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak] makes their realizations weak homotopy equivalences. Bijections on components and isomorphisms on all homotopy groups then transfer weak contractibility in both directions.

source.place: Proposition 4.7.3.20, identity edge and opposite-category dual of the final-slice criterion

proof.text: The explicit degreewise description of $P_x$ in Step 3 is exactly the one in [lem-coef-infinity-twisted-pullback-identity-initial], and Step 3 verified its quasicategory hypothesis. Apply that node to $\operatorname{id}_x$ to obtain its initiality in $P_x$. Step 3 shows $u$ is a map over $\mathcal C$ between left fibrations and carries $\operatorname{id}_x$ to itself; Step 4 gives its initiality in the domain. Consequently [lem-coef-infinity-left-fibration-initial-equivalence] applies with $E=\mathcal C_{x/}$, $F=P_x$, $B=\mathcal C$, and $e=\operatorname{id}_x$. It gives the claimed equivalence over $\mathcal C$ for this actual collapse map.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.2.10, application of initiality (03JW) and the left-fibration criterion (03J6)

proof.text: Apply the source-fixed result of Steps 3–5 to $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $y$. Ordered reversal identifies $(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}})_{y/}$ with $(\mathcal C_{/y})^{\mathrm{op}}$. There is a simplicial isomorphism $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}})\cong\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)$: interpret a map $N(J_n)\to\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ as a map $N(J_n)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ and precompose by the order isomorphism $J_n\to J_n^{\mathrm{op}}$ exchanging $\bar j$ and $j$. It commutes with every $\theta^{\mathrm{op}}\star\theta$, and exchanges the two block projections. Therefore it takes the source-fixed pullback for $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ to the target-fixed pullback for $\mathcal C$, over $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Under these two isomorphisms the first-block collapse becomes exactly the second-block collapse in the statement. This gives $(\mathcal C_{/y})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)\times_{\mathcal C}\{y\}$ as an equivalence over $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$. The order reversal and collapse leave the degenerate identity edge fixed.

source.place: Remark 8.1.1.7, duality isomorphism (without an extra opposite on Tw), applied to Proposition 8.1.2.10

proof.text: For a simplicial functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, postcomposition sends every defining map on $N(J_n)$ to its composite with $F$. This defines $\operatorname{Tw}(F)$ over $F^{\mathrm{op}}\times F$. For either block-collapse order map $c$, associativity gives $F\circ(\sigma\circ N(c))=(F\circ\sigma)\circ N(c)$ in every degree. These equalities commute with all simplicial operators, so both slice comparisons commute with $F$ strictly. A degenerate edge at $x$ is sent to the degenerate edge at $F(x)$, which proves the identity and functoriality clauses.
